subject: biology
note: A-level concepts. Each has its own note, never shared with GCSE or IGCSE. Merged by conceptMap.ts. Each A-level spec point is primary in exactly one concept.

concepts.title: Water and inorganic ions
concepts.scope: Hydrogen bonding and the properties of water that matter to life, the elements in biological molecules, and the roles of key inorganic ions.

concepts.title: Carbohydrates
concepts.scope: Monomers and polymers, alpha and beta glucose, ribose, condensation and hydrolysis of glycosidic bonds, and how starch, glycogen and cellulose suit their functions.

concepts.title: Lipids
concepts.scope: Triglycerides and phospholipids: structure, ester bonds, saturated versus unsaturated fatty acids, and how structure relates to function.

concepts.title: Proteins
concepts.scope: Amino acids and peptide bonds, the four levels of protein structure and the bonds that hold them, and globular versus fibrous proteins such as haemoglobin and collagen.

concepts.title: Testing for biological molecules and chromatography
concepts.scope: Qualitative and semi-quantitative tests for sugars, starch, lipids and proteins, colorimetry and calibration curves, and paper and thin layer chromatography.

concepts.title: How enzymes work
concepts.scope: Enzymes as globular catalysts, intracellular and extracellular enzymes, activation energy, specificity, and the lock-and-key and induced-fit models.

concepts.title: Factors affecting enzyme activity
concepts.scope: How temperature, pH, enzyme and substrate concentration change rate, Vmax and Km, cofactors and coenzymes, and competitive and non-competitive inhibition.

concepts.title: Microscopy
concepts.scope: Light and electron microscopes, slide preparation and staining, biological drawings, magnification and resolution, and measuring with an eyepiece graticule.

concepts.title: Eukaryotic cell ultrastructure
concepts.scope: Organelles of animal and plant cells, recognising them in electron micrographs, the cytoskeleton, and how the rER and Golgi produce and secrete proteins.

concepts.title: Prokaryotic cells and viruses
concepts.scope: The structure of prokaryotic cells compared with eukaryotic cells, and viruses as non-cellular particles.

concepts.title: The cell cycle and mitosis
concepts.scope: Chromosome structure, the stages of the cell cycle and mitosis, cell cycle regulation, telomeres, binary fission and how uncontrolled division causes tumours.

concepts.title: Meiosis, gametes and fertilisation
concepts.scope: Haploid and diploid cells, the stages of meiosis, how crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilisation create variation, and mammalian gametes and fertilisation.

concepts.title: Stem cells and cell specialisation
concepts.scope: Totipotent, pluripotent and multipotent stem cells, differentiation into specialised cells, tissues, organs and systems, and stem cell therapies.

concepts.title: Cell membranes and cell signalling
concepts.scope: The fluid mosaic model, the roles of phospholipids, cholesterol, glycoproteins and proteins, factors affecting permeability, and receptors in cell signalling.

concepts.title: Diffusion, active transport and bulk transport
concepts.scope: Simple and facilitated diffusion, active transport and co-transport, endocytosis and exocytosis, and the role of carrier and channel proteins.

concepts.title: Osmosis and water potential
concepts.scope: Water potential, osmosis in plant and animal cells, and estimating the water potential of plant tissue.

concepts.title: Surface area to volume ratio and exchange surfaces
concepts.scope: Why larger organisms need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems, and the features of an efficient exchange surface.

concepts.title: Gas exchange in mammals
concepts.scope: The structure of the human gas exchange system and its tissues, Fick's law, ventilation, and measuring lung volumes with a spirometer.

concepts.title: Gas exchange in fish, insects and plants
concepts.scope: Ventilation and gas exchange in bony fish and insects, and gas exchange in leaves, with adaptations that limit water loss.

concepts.title: Digestion and absorption
concepts.scope: The digestion of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins by enzymes, and how the products are absorbed across the ileum.

concepts.title: Circulatory systems, blood vessels and tissue fluid
concepts.scope: Open, closed, single and double circulation, the structure of arteries, veins and capillaries, blood cells, and the formation of tissue fluid.

concepts.title: The heart and the cardiac cycle
concepts.scope: The structure of the mammalian heart, pressure and volume changes in the cardiac cycle, and how valves control blood flow.

concepts.title: Control of the heartbeat and ECGs
concepts.scope: The SAN, AVN and Purkyne fibres, ECG traces, cardiac output, and how nerves and hormones change heart rate and breathing.

concepts.title: Haemoglobin and gas transport
concepts.scope: How haemoglobin carries oxygen, the oxygen dissociation curve, the Bohr shift, fetal haemoglobin, and carbon dioxide transport and the chloride shift.

concepts.title: Cardiovascular disease and health risk
concepts.scope: Atherosclerosis, blood clotting, risk factors including cholesterol and diet, treatments, and how to interpret health risk data and studies.

concepts.title: Plant transport tissues and fibres
concepts.scope: Why plants need transport systems, the structure and distribution of xylem, phloem and sclerenchyma, and the uses of plant fibres and starch.

concepts.title: Water transport and transpiration
concepts.scope: Water uptake and the apoplast and symplast pathways, transpiration and the cohesion-tension theory, stomata and guard cells, and xerophyte adaptations.

concepts.title: Translocation in the phloem
concepts.scope: Movement of assimilates from source to sink, active loading by companion cells, and the mass flow hypothesis.

concepts.title: Pathogens and disease transmission
concepts.scope: Types of pathogen, the diseases they cause including cholera, malaria, TB and HIV, how they spread and how their spread is controlled.

concepts.title: Non-specific defences
concepts.scope: Physical and chemical barriers, inflammation, phagocytosis, and defences of plants against pathogens.

concepts.title: The specific immune response
concepts.scope: Antigens, B and T lymphocytes, antibodies and their actions, primary and secondary responses, memory cells and autoimmune disease.

concepts.title: Vaccination and types of immunity
concepts.scope: Active, passive, natural and artificial immunity, how vaccines and vaccination programmes work, and the evolutionary race between pathogens and hosts.

concepts.title: Monoclonal antibodies
concepts.scope: How monoclonal antibodies are made by the hybridoma method and used in diagnosis, treatment and ELISA tests.

concepts.title: Antibiotics and medicines
concepts.scope: How antibiotics work, antibiotic resistance and hospital infections, sources of new medicines and how drugs are tested.

concepts.title: Nucleotides and the structure of DNA and RNA
concepts.scope: Nucleotide structure, phosphodiester bonds, base pairing in the DNA double helix, RNA structure and DNA purification.

concepts.title: DNA replication
concepts.scope: Semi-conservative replication, the roles of DNA helicase and DNA polymerase, and the Meselson and Stahl evidence.

concepts.title: Genes, chromosomes and the genetic code
concepts.scope: What a gene is, how DNA is packaged in chromosomes, and the triplet, non-overlapping, degenerate and universal genetic code.

concepts.title: Transcription and translation
concepts.scope: How mRNA is transcribed and spliced, and how ribosomes and tRNA translate it into a polypeptide.

concepts.title: Gene mutations
concepts.scope: Substitution, insertion and deletion mutations, mutagens, and how mutations change protein structure and function.

concepts.title: Control of gene expression
concepts.scope: Structural and regulatory genes, the lac operon, transcription factors, gibberellin and DELLA proteins, and post-transcriptional control including RNAi.

concepts.title: Epigenetics and cancer
concepts.scope: DNA methylation and histone modification, how environment changes gene expression, and the role of oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes in cancer.

concepts.title: Genetic control of body plans
concepts.scope: Homeobox genes controlling body plans, and how mitosis and apoptosis shape body form.

concepts.title: Monohybrid inheritance
concepts.scope: Genes, alleles, genotype and phenotype, dominance and codominance, multiple alleles, and genetic diagrams for monohybrid and test crosses.

concepts.title: Dihybrid crosses, linkage, epistasis and chi-squared
concepts.scope: Dihybrid inheritance, sex linkage, autosomal linkage and epistasis, and using the chi-squared test to compare observed and expected ratios.

concepts.title: Variation: genes, environment and phenotype
concepts.scope: Continuous and discontinuous variation, polygenic inheritance, how genes and the environment shape phenotype, and examples of genes affecting proteins.

concepts.title: Cystic fibrosis and genetic screening
concepts.scope: How cystic fibrosis affects the body, carrier and prenatal screening, DNA probes, and the ethical issues of screening and gene therapy.

concepts.title: Natural and artificial selection
concepts.scope: Adaptation, natural selection and its types, evidence for evolution, antibiotic resistance as an example, and selective breeding.

concepts.title: Population genetics and the Hardy-Weinberg principle
concepts.scope: Gene pools and allele frequencies, genetic drift and the founder effect, and using the Hardy-Weinberg equation.

concepts.title: Speciation
concepts.scope: How geographical and reproductive isolation lead to allopatric and sympatric speciation.

concepts.title: Classification and phylogeny
concepts.scope: Species concepts, the taxonomic hierarchy, binomial names, the three domains and five kingdoms, and using DNA and protein sequences to find relationships.

concepts.title: Measuring biodiversity
concepts.scope: Biodiversity at habitat, species and genetic level, species richness and evenness, Simpson's index, heterozygosity and the threat from human activity.

concepts.title: Conservation
concepts.scope: Causes of extinction, reasons to conserve, in situ and ex situ conservation, seed banks and zoos, international agreements, and managing ecosystems sustainably.

concepts.title: ATP
concepts.scope: The structure of ATP, its hydrolysis and synthesis, and why it is the universal energy currency.

concepts.title: Chloroplasts and photosynthetic pigments
concepts.scope: The overall reaction of photosynthesis, chloroplast structure, pigments, absorption and action spectra, and separating pigments by chromatography.

concepts.title: The light-dependent reactions
concepts.scope: Photosystems, photolysis, cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation, and the production of ATP and reduced NADP by chemiosmosis.

concepts.title: The Calvin cycle
concepts.scope: Carbon fixation by rubisco, the reduction of GP to triose phosphate, regeneration of RuBP, and uses of triose phosphate.

concepts.title: Limiting factors of photosynthesis
concepts.scope: How light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature limit the rate, and how to investigate them.

concepts.title: Glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle
concepts.scope: Why organisms need energy, mitochondrial structure, and the stages, sites and products of glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle.

concepts.title: Oxidative phosphorylation
concepts.scope: The electron transport chain, chemiosmosis and ATP synthase, and the role of oxygen as the final electron acceptor.

concepts.title: Anaerobic respiration
concepts.scope: Lactate and ethanol fermentation, what happens to lactate, why aerobic respiration yields more ATP, and rice adaptations to flooding.

concepts.title: Respiratory substrates, RQ and respiration rate
concepts.scope: Energy values of respiratory substrates, the respiratory quotient, and measuring respiration with respirometers and redox indicators.

concepts.title: Ecosystems, populations and succession
concepts.scope: Ecosystems, niches, biotic and abiotic factors, competition and predation, carrying capacity, and succession to a climax community.

concepts.title: Sampling and estimating populations
concepts.scope: Random and systematic sampling with quadrats and transects, and estimating population size by mark-release-recapture.

concepts.title: Energy transfer and productivity
concepts.scope: Gross and net primary productivity, energy transfer between trophic levels, and how farming practices increase efficiency.

concepts.title: Nutrient cycles and decomposition
concepts.scope: The carbon and nitrogen cycles, the role of microorganisms and decomposition, using decomposition to estimate time of death, and fertilisers and eutrophication.

concepts.title: Climate change
concepts.scope: Evidence for climate change, the greenhouse effect, the limits of models, and effects on plants and animals.

concepts.title: Receptors and neurones
concepts.scope: Sensory, relay and motor neurones, myelination, and how receptors such as the Pacinian corpuscle, taste buds and rod cells turn stimuli into impulses.

concepts.title: Nerve impulses
concepts.scope: Resting and action potentials, the refractory period, saltatory conduction, and factors affecting conduction speed.

concepts.title: Synapses and drugs
concepts.scope: Cholinergic synapses, summation and inhibition, and how drugs and chemical imbalances affect synaptic transmission.

concepts.title: The nervous system, brain and responses
concepts.scope: Organisation of the nervous system, regions of the brain, reflexes, taxes and kineses, the pupil reflex, and nervous versus hormonal coordination.

concepts.title: Brain development and research
concepts.scope: Brain imaging, the critical period in vision, animal models and their ethics, habituation, and nature versus nurture in brain development.

concepts.title: Muscle contraction
concepts.scope: Skeletal muscle structure, the neuromuscular junction, the sliding filament model, and fast and slow twitch fibres.

concepts.title: Exercise, sport and health
concepts.scope: Effects of too much or too little exercise, medical technology in sport, and ethics of performance-enhancing drugs.

concepts.title: Principles of homeostasis and thermoregulation
concepts.scope: Negative and positive feedback, cell signalling, and temperature control in ectotherms and endotherms.

concepts.title: Hormones and blood glucose
concepts.scope: The endocrine system and adrenal glands, insulin and glucagon, second messengers, diabetes and its treatment, and glucose biosensors.

concepts.title: The liver and excretion
concepts.scope: Excretion, the liver and deamination, kidney failure and its treatment, and urine in diagnosis.

concepts.title: The kidney and osmoregulation
concepts.scope: Nephron structure, ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption, the loop of Henle, and control of blood water potential by ADH.

concepts.title: Plant responses and hormones
concepts.scope: Tropisms, auxin, gibberellins, abscisic acid and phytochrome, rapid responses such as the Venus fly trap, and commercial uses of plant hormones.

concepts.title: Genome sequencing and bioinformatics
concepts.scope: DNA sequencing methods, genome projects, comparing genomes and proteomes, microarrays, sequence databases and personalised medicine.

concepts.title: PCR, electrophoresis and DNA profiling
concepts.scope: Amplifying DNA by PCR, separating fragments by gel electrophoresis, and using DNA profiles for identification and relationships.

concepts.title: Recombinant DNA technology
concepts.scope: Isolating genes, restriction enzymes, ligase, vectors, promoters and marker genes, gene editing, and making recombinant proteins.

concepts.title: Gene therapy and GMOs
concepts.scope: Gene therapy, genetically modified crops and animals for food, and the ethical and social issues they raise.

concepts.title: Cloning
concepts.scope: Natural and artificial cloning in plants and animals, including cuttings, tissue culture, embryo twinning and SCNT.

concepts.title: Microorganisms and enzymes in biotechnology
concepts.scope: Culturing microorganisms aseptically, batch and continuous fermentation, growth curves, food production, and immobilised enzymes.

concepts.title: Planning and evaluating experiments
concepts.scope: Designing investigations, identifying and controlling variables, safety and ethics, keeping records, research and citations, and evaluating methods and results.

concepts.title: Data handling and statistics
concepts.scope: Units, significant figures, graphs, processing data, and choosing and using statistical tests such as the t-test and correlation coefficients.

concepts.title: Laboratory techniques and apparatus
concepts.scope: Using measuring apparatus, colorimeters, potometers, serial dilutions, microscopes, chromatography, electrophoresis, aseptic technique and dissection.

concepts.title: Core practicals: biochemistry and enzymes
concepts.scope: Vitamin C content, enzyme concentration and initial rate, temperature and Q10, and following enzyme reactions with catalase, amylase and a colorimeter.

concepts.title: Core practicals: cells and physiology
concepts.scope: Daphnia heart rate, membrane permeability, root tip squash, respiration rate, spirometer traces and habituation.

concepts.title: Core practicals: plants, microbes and ecology
concepts.scope: Plant tissues and fibres, mineral deficiencies, antimicrobial properties and antibiotics, the Hill reaction, development and temperature, gel electrophoresis and field ecology.
